# SiteCheck — SunshineCTF 2026 (web, 500 pts)

**Flag:** `sun{fr4gm3nt3d_r3fl3ct10ns_1n_th3_futur3}`

## Challenge summary

> SiteCheck is a "web-diagnostics service": you enlist, submit any http(s) URL,
> and an autonomous "inspection drone" flies out to it, times the load, counts
> the resources, and beams back a viewport screenshot.
>
> "The drone politely refuses to inspect internal or local addresses."

The service lives at `https://spaceship.web.2026.sunshinectf.games`.

## Recon

Registering an account (`POST /register` with `username`, `password`, `viewport`)
lands you on `/dashboard`, which has a single form: `POST /scan` with a `url`
field. A successful scan 302-redirects to `/result/<uuid>`, which shows:

- status code, load time, number of files fetched
- a **screenshot** of the page the drone rendered (`/screenshots/<uuid>.png`)
- any error from the drone — notably raw Playwright messages such as
  `page.goto: net::ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED at ...`, confirming the drone is a
  headless Chromium driven by Playwright.

## Vulnerability 1: SSRF with an incomplete filter

Probing the URL filter:

| URL | Result |
|---|---|
| `http://127.0.0.1/` | blocked |
| `http://localhost/` | blocked |
| `http://0.0.0.0/` | blocked |
| `http://127.1/`, `http://2130706433/`, `http://0x7f000001/` | blocked |
| `http://[::1]/` | **allowed** (connection refused — nothing on :80) |
| `http://169.254.169.254/...` | **allowed** (GCP metadata 403/404) |

The filter enumerates IPv4 loopback spellings but never considers **IPv6
loopback**. Everything after this goes through `http://[::1]/`.

(The box is a GCE instance — `169.254.169.254` answers. The v1 metadata API
returns 403 without the `Metadata-Flavor: Google` header, which a plain
`page.goto` can't set, so that path dead-ends.)

## Challenge summary

> Tomorrow-Mart sells used goods; a FutureBank account comes with 500 free
> credits. The grand prize — the deed to the Founders' Vault (Lot #4042) —
> costs 1,000,000 credits. Category hint: `jex`.

Service: `https://usedgoods.web.2026.sunshinectf.games/` (GraphQL at `/graphql`).

## Recon

The storefront is a thin JS client over a GraphQL API (`POST /graphql`,
`Authorization: Bearer <token>`). Useful introspection queries work, so the
schema can be mapped:

**Query fields:** `listings`, `listing(id)`, `myAccount`, `promoCodes(vendorKey: String!)`

**Mutation fields:**

| field | args | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `register` / `login` | `username`, `password` | returns `{token}` |
| `placeOrder` | `listingId: ID!`, `promoCode: String` | returns `{success message pricePaid flag}` |
| `vendorTerminalSync` | `terminalId: ID` | returns `{terminalId status firmware vendorKey note}` |

`placeOrder` on the Vault Deed without a promo correctly fails — 500 credits
won't cover 1,000,000.

Promo codes are pure lookup values (`SCOUT-10` = -10%); `promoCode` is *not*
an expression-injection sink, so the `jex` hint points elsewhere — at the
vendor terminal machinery.

 🔍 "> Build Your Badge Security BSides Orlando 2026 Build Your Badge Your badge arrives part-built. Seven pieces are yours to solder — here's how to do it on your own, at your own pace, without queuing at the Soldering Village. What's in your kit Everything else — the microcontroller, the reverse-mounted LEDs, all the tiny parts — is already soldered on when you pick the badge up. 4× LED goes on the front 1× SAO connector goes on the front 1× Power switch goes on the back 1× Battery holder goes on the back 1× AAA battery no soldering A suggested order Not a rule, just the order that keeps the board flattest and easiest to hold while you work — lowest parts first, tallest last. Power switch — back The only surface-mount piece, and the fiddliest. Do it while the board is still completely flat. Tack one corner pad, check the switch sits square against the printing, then solder the rest. The four LEDs — front Push them in from the front so the bodies stick out the art side, then turn the badge over and solder the legs on the back. Trim the legs afterwards. SAO connector — front Also fits from the front and solders from behind, so add-ons plug into the art side. Battery holder — back Tallest part, so it goes last. Sits on the back, soldered from the front. Battery in, switch to ON Drop the AAA into the holder and slide the switch to ON . Three things worth slowing down for The SAO notch faces up The six-pin socket only works one way round — notch toward the top edge of the badge. Fitted backwards, anything you plug into it gets power and ground swapped. It's printed on the back of the board if you want to double-check. Square pad takes the short leg Each LED has one square pad and one round one. The square pad takes the shorter leg — the one on the flat side of the LED body. Backwards, the LED simply never lights. # SiteCheck — SunshineCTF 2026 (web, 500 pts)

**Flag:** `sun{fr4gm3nt3d_r3fl3ct10ns_1n_th3_futur3}`

## Challenge summary

> SiteCheck is a "web-diagnostics service": you enlist, submit any http(s) URL,
> and an autonomous "inspection drone" flies out to it, times the load, counts
> the resources, and beams back a viewport screenshot.
>
> "The drone politely refuses to inspect internal or local addresses."

The service lives at `https://spaceship.web.2026.sunshinectf.games`.

## Recon

Registering an account (`POST /register` with `username`, `password`, `viewport`)
lands you on `/dashboard`, which has a single form: `POST /scan` with a `url`
field. A successful scan 302-redirects to `/result/<uuid>`, which shows:

- status code, load time, number of files fetched
- a **screenshot** of the page the drone rendered (`/screenshots/<uuid>.png`)
- any error from the drone — notably raw Playwright messages such as
  `page.goto: net::ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED at ...`, confirming the drone is a
  headless Chromium driven by Playwright.

## Vulnerability 1: SSRF with an incomplete filter

Probing the URL filter:

| URL | Result |
|---|---|
| `http://127.0.0.1/` | blocked |
| `http://localhost/` | blocked |
| `http://0.0.0.0/` | blocked |
| `http://127.1/`, `http://2130706433/`, `http://0x7f000001/` | blocked |
| `http://[::1]/` | **allowed** (connection refused — nothing on :80) |
| `http://169.254.169.254/...` | **allowed** (GCP metadata 403/404) |

The filter enumerates IPv4 loopback spellings but never considers **IPv6
loopback**. Everything after this goes through `http://[::1]/`.

(The box is a GCE instance — `169.254.169.254` answers. The v1 metadata API
returns 403 without the `Metadata-Flavor: Google` header, which a plain
`page.goto` can't set, so that path dead-ends.)

## Vulnerability 2: the drone is authenticated as admin

Port-scanning `[::1]` through the drone (each probe is one `/scan` request):

# SiteCheck — SunshineCTF 2026 (web, 500 pts)

**Flag:** `sun{fr4gm3nt3d_r3fl3ct10ns_1n_th3_futur3}`

## Challenge summary

> SiteCheck is a "web-diagnostics service": you enlist, submit any http(s) URL,
> and an autonomous "inspection drone" flies out to it, times the load, counts
> the resources, and beams back a viewport screenshot.
>
> "The drone politely refuses to inspect internal or local addresses."

The service lives at `https://spaceship.web.2026.sunshinectf.games`.

## Recon

Registering an account (`POST /register` with `username`, `password`, `viewport`)
lands you on `/dashboard`, which has a single form: `POST /scan` with a `url`
field. A successful scan 302-redirects to `/result/<uuid>`, which shows:

- status code, load time, number of files fetched
- a **screenshot** of the page the drone rendered (`/screenshots/<uuid>.png`)

loopback**. Everything after this goes through `http://[::1]/`.

Seven pieces are yours to solder — here's how to do it on your own, at your own pace, without queuing at the Soldering Village. What's in your kit Everything else — the microcontroller, the reverse-mounted LEDs, all the tiny parts — is already soldered on when you pick the badge up. 4× LED goes on the front 1× SAO connector goes on the front 1× Power switch goes on the back 1× Battery holder goes on the back 1× AAA battery no soldering A suggested order Not a rule, just the order that keeps the board flattest and easiest to hold while you work — lowest parts first, tallest last. Power switch — back The only surface-mount piece, and the fiddliest. Do it while the board is still completely flat. Tack one corner pad, check the switch sits square against the printing, then solder the rest. The four LEDs — front Push them in from the front so the bodies stick out the art side, then turn the badge over and solder the legs on the back. Trim the legs afterwards. SAO connector — front Also fits from the front and solders from behind, so add-ons plug into the art side. Battery holder — back Tallest part, so it goes last. Sits on the back, soldered from the front. Battery in, switch to ON Drop the AAA into the holder and slide the switch to ON . Three things worth slowing down for The SAO notch faces up The six-pin socket only works one way round — notch toward the top edge of the badge. Fitted backwards, anything you plug into it gets power and ground swapped. It's printed on the back of the board if you want to double-check. Square pad takes the short leg Each LED has one square pad and one round one. The square pad takes the shorter leg — the one on the flat side of the LED body. Backwards, the LED simply never lights. {"command": "cd /challenge/workspace && python3 - <<'EOF'
d=open('bg-repo/hardware/uv_art.psd','rb').read()
print('size',len(d))
import re
# find all luni tags and following names
idx=0
names=[]
while True:
    i=d.find(b'8BIMluni',idx)
    if i<0: break
    # after 8BIMluni, 4 bytes length, then UTF-16 name padded to 4
    ln=int.from_bytes(d[i+8:i+12],'big')
    raw=d[i+12:i+12+ln]
    try:
        nm=raw.decode('utf-16-be')
    except: nm=repr(raw)
    names.append(nm)
    idx=i+12

{"command": "cd /challenge/workspace && python3 - <<'EOF'
from PIL import Image
import numpy as np
# uv_art content bbox via alpha
uv=Image.open('uv_art.png')
a=np.array(uv.split()[-1])  # alpha
ys,xs=np.where(a>10)
print('uv alpha bbox', xs.min(),xs.max(),ys.min(),ys.max())
uvc=uv.crop((xs.min(),ys.min(),xs.max()+1,ys.max()+1)).convert('L')
uvc.save('uvc.png'); print('uvc',uvc.size)

# logo content
logo=Image.open('LOGO_DWGS.png').convert('L')
arr=np.array(logo)
ys2,xs2=np.where(arr<128)
print('logo bbox', xs2.min(),xs2.max(),ys2.min(),ys2.max())
lg=logo.crop((xs2.min(),ys2.min(),xs2.max()+1,ys2.max()+1)).transpose(Image.FLIP_LEFT_RIGHT)
lg.save('lg.png'); print('lg',lg.size)
lgr=lg.resize(uvc.size)
lgr.save('lgr.png')
A=np.array(uvc).astype(int); B=np.array(lgr).astype(int)
d=np.abs(A-B)
print('mean',d.mean(),'frac>80',(d>80).mean())
Image.fromarray((d).clip(0,255).astype('uint8')).save('ARTDIFF.png')
EOF
ls -la uvc.png lg.png ARTDIFF.png", "timeout_seconds": 60}
